solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Destroyed a large ring of ox-wagons

indicators.note: whatever is destroyed is knocked apart, so its letters fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A huge circle of wagons has been wrecked, as if after a battle on the veld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyed' reads as a verb acting on the ring, but it only works on the next two words. LAAGER is an Afrikaans word for a defensive encampment.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager is the South African term for a defensive camp formed by drawing wagons into a circle.

clue.text: Some other culprit turned up the spoils

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying inside the words
in a down clue, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a run straddling the two words, read upwards in the grid

explanation.surface: A second offender has turned up with the stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'other culprit' backwards and LUCRE sits inside it: otHER CULprit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or profit, usually ill-gotten, much like the gains or loot taken in plunder.

clue.text: In American university Queen songs tanks

indicators.note: one thing set in another is held inside it

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
Q is the abbreviation for queen, as on playing cards
U is the abbreviation for university
an aria is an operatic solo song

explanation.surface: A rock band's songs being played on an American campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock band, but it is just Q, placed inside A U; songs then follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria is a plural of aquarium, the glass tanks in which fish and other water creatures are kept.

clue.text: No mistakes here for Rupert Everett — thrice initially troubled

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the named words
something troubled is stirred up and disturbed, so the letters are put in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
the English actor's initials
the same pair of initials twice more, making three times in all

explanation.surface: A worried actor is pleased that this time his performance had no slips.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Everett is the English actor; his initials R and E, taken three times, join FOR to make the letters for ERROR-FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something error-free is flawless, the definition read as a description of a perfect piece of work.

clue.text: Enemy threats to a sub at sea

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be confused and all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Hostile dangers facing a submarine out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link between definition and wordplay, but its letters are part of what is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: U-boats were German submarines, a deadly menace to Allied shipping in both world wars.

clue.text: Waits for former president’s name dropping

indicators.note: dropping something lets it go, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: Joe Biden, a former US president, with the possessive S
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone hangs around waiting for an ex-president's name to come up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waits for' reads as one phrase, but 'for' is only a link; the N comes out of BIDEN'S.
explanation.definitionFit: To bide is to wait or remain, as in biding one's time until a chance arrives.

clue.text: Broken coat-hangers gone missing on refuse truck

indicators.note: what has gone missing is no longer there, so those letters are taken away
something broken is in pieces, so what is left is put back in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
these four letters are removed, one by one, from the fodder

explanation.surface: Bent wire coat-hangers have disappeared onto the bin lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike G, O, N and E from COATHANGERS to leave CATHARS, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash cart was the old horse-drawn vehicle collecting household ashes and rubbish, the forerunner of the bin lorry.

clue.text: Drama coach with freedom of movement

blocks.note: a stagecoach, or stage for short, is a horse-drawn coach
play is the slack or freedom a moving part has

explanation.surface: An acting teacher who lets students move about freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama coach' looks like a single phrase for an acting tutor; split it, and the coach is the old horse-drawn stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage-play is a drama written for performance in a theatre rather than for radio or screen.

clue.text: Get a 100 and 24 sheets of paper

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a quire is a paper measure of 24 sheets

explanation.surface: Scoring a hundred in an exam and picking up a stack of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a traditional paper measure (24 or 25 sheets; 20 quires make a ream).
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire is to obtain or come to possess, a plain synonym of the verb in the clue.

clue.text: Statesman arranged aid with disheartened hooligan

indicators.note: arranged means put into a chosen order, so the letters are reordered
losing one's heart means the central part is taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
the word with its central four letters removed

explanation.surface: A politician has organised help along with a dispirited thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' suggests a politician, but here it is a man from a US state. HOOLIGAN loses OLIG from its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An Idahoan is a native of Idaho, so quite literally a man of one American state.

clue.text: Brecht’s collaborator provides short, disagreeable sounds

indicators.note: sounds asks for what is heard rather than what is written

blocks.note: curt means brief or abrupt
vile means nasty; the German surname is said with a V sound

explanation.surface: A playwright's partner turns out to be making brief, unpleasant noises.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is the German pronunciation: Weill is said 'vile', so 'curt, vile' spoken aloud gives the composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurt Weill was the German composer who wrote the music for Bertolt Brecht's The Threepenny Opera.

clue.text: Lords’ cliques who have much in common

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'those who', where the answer is a plural noun

blocks.note: lords are peers of the realm
cliques are small exclusive groups

explanation.surface: Factions in the House of Lords made up of like-minded members.
explanation.walkthrough: A peer is a member of the House of Lords, the upper chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Peer groups are sets of people of similar age, status or interests, who share a lot.

clue.text: Some cafe with sandwiches

indicators.note: to sandwich is to enclose between layers, so the answer sits held inside

blocks.note: a run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A coffee shop that serves a handful of sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' reads as food on the menu, but it is a verb: the two words enclose the answer, cAFE With.
explanation.definitionFit: A few means a small number of, the same quantifier sense as the word some.

clue.text: Sports car and a Roller at my island’s ferry port

blocks.note: MG is a classic British sports car marque
taken as written
a Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce, abbreviated RR

explanation.surface: Smart cars queue at the harbour to board the ferry to the setter's home island.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym is Gozo, so 'my island' is Gozo, the Maltese island whose ferries dock at Mgarr.
explanation.definitionFit: Mgarr is the harbour town on Gozo where the ferries from mainland Malta arrive and depart.

clue.text: Autobiography of member — fame and kin involved

indicators.note: involved means intricate and tangled, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: MP, a Member of Parliament
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician's memoir, full of celebrity and family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Autobiography of member' looks like the definition, but 'of' is a link and the member gives MP for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Mein Kampf is Hitler's autobiographical manifesto, written in prison in the 1920s.

clue.text: Accelerator and choke

blocks.note: first meaning: the control regulating fuel to an engine
second meaning: to strangle someone

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as two car controls, since a choke is also a carburettor valve; the second definition is the strangling verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the engine's fuel control, while the verb means to grip someone's throat and strangle them.

clue.text: Five painters redesigned panel-fastening joint

indicators.note: a redesign gives a new layout, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of five artists has reworked a design for joining panels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five' is a number in the surface but just the Roman numeral V in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet snap is the domed head of a rivet, or the tool shaping it, holding metal panels together.

clue.text: Divisions of motorway to east of Italian city

blocks.note: the M1, written MI in crosswords, is Britain's main north-south motorway
lanes are the strips a road is divided into
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Lanes of a motorway heading east from an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords. 'of Italian city' is an adjective phrase, so the answer is the adjective for Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Milanese is the adjective for things from Milan, the city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Hillman marque for Steed or Purdey

blocks.note: first meaning: a 1970s British family saloon made by Hillman
second meaning: a secret agent from the 1960s-70s British TV series

explanation.walkthrough: Hillman was a British car maker; John Steed and Purdey were agents in the TV series The Avengers, so each is one avenger.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a Hillman saloon car and a member of the television spy team in The Avengers.

clue.text: Initially Jeremy Vine backed Sir Robin on August 15 1945

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words that follow
backed means moved backwards, so the order is turned round

blocks.note: the broadcaster's initials
Sir Robin Day was a famous British political interviewer

explanation.surface: One broadcaster backing another on an historic date.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Vine and Sir Robin Day are both BBC presenters, which makes 'backed' look like support rather than a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: VJ Day, Victory over Japan Day, marked Japan's surrender ending the Second World War.

clue.text: Resident departs with Dickens’ Sam

blocks.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in The Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A tenant leaves in the company of a character from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces rather than giving W; WELLER already brings its own W.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller is someone who lives in a particular place, a plain synonym for an inhabitant.

clue.text: Channel broadcasting cricket to eastern isle

blocks.note: Sky Sports holds the main TV rights to English cricket
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A TV channel showing cricket to viewers on an island in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is the British satellite broadcaster; Skye is an island off the west coast of Scotland, so 'eastern' only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, in western Scotland.

clue.text: Grants for rented gardening plots

blocks.note: first meaning: shares given out or assigned
second meaning: small plots of council land let for growing vegetables

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an allotment is a small plot of land rented from the local council for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both portions allocated to someone and the rented strips of land for gardening.

clue.text: Manx recluse regularly performing ice-skating feats

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A hermit from the Isle of Man is out on the ice doing jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'Manx recluse' are taken: mAnX rEcLuSe.
explanation.definitionFit: An axel is a figure-skating jump with a forward take-off and one and a half turns in the air.

clue.text: They could be spare in city restaurant

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the words that follow

blocks.note: a run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Diners who might be surplus to requirements in an urban eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare' suggests extra people; it is the spare wheel kept in a car boot. The answer runs across ciTY RESTaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is the extra one carried in a car, so tyres could be spare ones.

clue.text: Asylum seekers from corrupt regimes

indicators.note: something corrupt is spoiled and distorted, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Refugees fleeing crooked governments.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is so plausible that 'from corrupt regimes' reads as description, not as instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Émigrés are people who have left their country, typically for political reasons, seeking refuge abroad.

clue.text: Bucks’ trophies?

blocks.note: surface reading: prizes won by young men, or by a team from Buckinghamshire
setter's reading: the bucks are male deer, and their trophies are what hunters mount on walls

explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire and a buck is also a dashing young man, so the clue suggests cups won; the bucks are male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag's or buck's branched horns are the classic hunting trophy, mounted on a wall.

clue.text: Leading medic has left wooded area

indicators.note: someone who has left is gone, so those letters are no longer present

blocks.note: foremost means first or in the lead
MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A senior doctor has walked off into the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading medic' looks like one person, a top doctor; split it, and the medic is MO, removed from the word for leading.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is a large area of land thickly covered with trees, a wooded area.

clue.text: Winds on peaks

definitions.note: the noun sense, coils or turns, not the verb

blocks.note: first meaning: coils or spiral turns
second meaning: tapering pointed tops, as on church towers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds on peaks' suggests mountain weather; a spire is also a single turn of a spiral or coil.
explanation.definitionFit: A spire is both a turn of a helix, as in a snail shell, and a tall tapering summit.
